## Download

[Download the latest wsiTools tissue visualizer skill (ZIP)](https://tkcaccia.github.io/wsiTools/downloads/wsi-tissue-visualizer.zip).

This skill gives Codex and other coding agents a tested way to build a focused,
read-only tissue visualization from a whole-slide image and optional GeoJSON.
The bundled builder uses wsiTools to generate full-resolution Deep Zoom tiles,
then writes a compact viewer with pan, zoom, class visibility, opacity, outlines,
and a scale bar when microns-per-pixel metadata is available. A second command
exports a bounded, high-resolution PNG figure or slide overview. It copies the
source GeoJSON exactly and leaves the slide and scored data unchanged.

The [source files](https://github.com/tkcaccia/wsiTools/tree/main/skills/wsi-tissue-visualizer)
can also be read directly on GitHub. The ZIP contains `SKILL.md`, the R builder,
the viewer template, a PNG renderer, a bundle verifier, and `SOURCE_VERSION.json` identifying
the wsiTools source revision used to build it.

## Install and use

Unzip the archive into `~/.codex/skills/` to let Codex discover
`wsi-tissue-visualizer/SKILL.md`. Other agents can read that file and run the
bundled scripts from the same directory. Building a viewer requires R with
wsiTools 0.1.28 or newer and libvips.

```sh
Rscript ~/.codex/skills/wsi-tissue-visualizer/scripts/build_viewer.R \
  --slide /absolute/path/slide.svs \
  --geojson /absolute/path/regions.geojson \
  --out /absolute/path/tissue-viewer \
  --title "Tissue review"

python3 ~/.codex/skills/wsi-tissue-visualizer/scripts/verify_bundle.py \
  /absolute/path/tissue-viewer

Rscript ~/.codex/skills/wsi-tissue-visualizer/scripts/render_figure.R \
  --slide /absolute/path/slide.svs \
  --geojson /absolute/path/regions.geojson \
  --x 10000 --y 20000 --width 6000 --height 4000 \
  --pixels 3000 --out /absolute/path/figure.png
```

Serve the output directory over HTTP to preview it, or publish its files on a
static host. GeoJSON coordinates must be level-0 slide pixels; if another
coordinate system was used, register it explicitly before visualization. PNG
export also requires the optional `magick` R package.

## Staying current

The [pkgdown site workflow](https://github.com/tkcaccia/wsiTools/blob/main/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
regenerates the download ZIP on every push to `main`. The ZIP includes a source
fingerprint and revision. A separate CI check compares the wsiTools APIs used by
the skill with reviewed source hashes. Changes to those APIs require the skill
to be checked and its API lock refreshed before the updated download is built.
This catches source changes that need a human or agent to adapt the skill's
instructions or scripts; a hash refresh alone does not prove behavior is sound.
